name: How much extra square footage do I actually need for a bathroom expansion in a small LA home?

mainEntity.name: How many extra square feet do I need to expand a bathroom without making the rest of the house feel cramped?
mainEntity.text: How many extra square feet do I need to expand a bathroom without making the rest of the house feel cramped?

acceptedAnswer.text: The right size increase depends on the goal of the remodel. If the bathroom only needs better movement and storage, a modest 15 to 25 square feet can make a big difference. If the plan includes a larger shower, double vanity, linen storage, or a more open primary bath, 30 to 40 or more additional square feet is often needed. In older Los Angeles-area homes, the biggest constraint is usually not the bathroom itself but the adjacent room layout, plumbing wall location, and structural framing. A smart expansion starts by measuring the existing fixture clearances and deciding which features matter most. If you want a true luxury feel, focus on layout efficiency before adding maximum square footage. That usually gives better results than simply making the room bigger. A designer or contractor should test several floor plans before construction so the added space improves function instead of creating wasted area.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bathroom expansion usually needs 15 to 40 extra square feet for a noticeable improvement, depending on whether you are adding a larger shower, double vanity, or separate tub. The right amount depends on the existing layout, hallway access, plumbing locations, and how much circulation space you want around fixtures.
